atoms.b: Shortly after the Battle of Stamford Bridge, King Harold received news that William had landed in the ((North ++South)) of England.
King Harold’s ((++tired relaxed)) army then had to march 185 miles in just four days to fight William.

instruction.text: Can you help prepare this Norman knight for battle? Drag his equipment to the correct places.

feedback.correct: Shields were used for protection. Knights held it in one hand to block attacks during battle.
Swords were used by knights to attack enemies.

instruction.text: Read the description and select the correct type of soldier.

atoms.a: This person uses a bow and arrow.

feedback.finish: In William’s army, archers fired arrows from far away and many Norman knights moved quickly on horses. Harold’s army all fought on foot and had never faced so many archers before!

instruction.text: Drag the features to the correct army.

feedback.finish: While the two armies were similar in size, William’s army was better-trained and more diverse.

atoms.b: Harold’s army lined up at the top of Senlac Hill and held their ((++shields hands)) close together to protect themselves from attack.
The English had a ((++strong weak)) position. William’s soldiers could not break through the English shield wall.
The shields blocked the Normans’ arrows, and it was difficult for the horses to ((++run fly)) uphill.

instruction.text: Listen and select the correct answer.

hint.text: This strategy is called a feigned retreat.
hint.label: Did you know?

atoms.a: William pretended to run away from battle. What do you think happened next?

b.sound: Harold’s soldiers chased after them and lost their defensive position.
William’s army ran all the way back to Normandy.

feedback.end: William’s trick worked! After Harold’s army broke their shield wall, they were unprotected and easy to attack. King Harold was killed in battle, and William won the Battle of Hastings.

instruction.text: Listen and select the correct answer.

atoms.a: What nickname did William get after winning the Battle of Hastings?

feedback.end: William the Conqueror didn’t just win the battle, he changed English history forever!
